Nicolas de Neufchâtel - Portrait of goldsmith Wenzel Jamnitzer (c. 1562-63)

Heavy symbolism going on here. This portrait is roughly based on the Tarot trump, the Magician. The man look a lot like John Dee, and indeed this was painted during Dee's lifetime. You've got a drafting compass, an hour glass (more like an egg timer, actually) a book, and a wand. The small wax figure to be cast into gold appears to be a Greek god, probably Posidon, god of the seas, since he is standing on a giant sea shell. The wand is, of course, an early form of the slide rule, and was used for computations. Notice that the man points with his left index finger at a pair of eyeglasses which do not seem to have any lenses. The flowers in the vase in the background are colorless, and may have been cast into silver. The wax figurine of the god is to be cast in purest gold, a kind of alchemical transmutation from wax to gold.
